# How to Run (Mac + VS Code) — graphs are generated by the code

## 1. One-time setup
```
cd path/to/traffic_gnn_final_modified/src
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install torch torch_geometric scapy scikit-learn matplotlib tqdm numpy
```
(The prompt must show `(venv)`. If you see "No module named torch", the venv is not active.)

## 2. Run everything and generate all graphs (recommended)
```
python3 run_end_to_end_demo.py
```
Takes about 10-15 minutes on CPU. It trains the base model and N1-N6, prints the
results table, and draws the graphs into the `plots/` folder.

## 3. Quick option (about 1 minute) — good for a live demo
```
python3 build_dataset.py
python3 build_hierarchical_dataset.py
python3 train_one.py base
python3 train_one.py n1
python3 train_one.py n5
```
Each `train_one.py` run redraws the graphs in `plots/` using the results so far.
(`n2` takes ~3 min and `n3` ~4 min if you want those too.)

## 4. Show the N1 fix
```
python3 adaptive_graph_builder.py
```
Prints `threshold_net grad norm ... (should be > 0)`.

## 5. Where are the graphs?
Open the `src/plots/` folder in VS Code and double-click a PNG:
- `1_model_comparison.png`    accuracy of every model
- `2_confusion_matrix.png`    base model mistakes
- `3_early_exit_tradeoff.png` N6 speed vs accuracy (appears after the full run)
- `4_graph_examples.png`      the traffic graphs themselves

To redraw without retraining: `python3 plot_results.py`

## Notes
- Real .pcap files: put them in `src/data/nonvpn/chat|email|streaming|voip/` and run the same commands.
- Numbers change a little on every run (random seeds). That is normal.
- A Python 3.14 "torch.jit.script" warning is harmless.
